## FIXED ON MAIN BY ANOTHER CHANGE — `36e986c188` "Cite f124 instead of a bare run id"

Verified against `gerrit/main`, not assumed: `python scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py` exits **0**,
and `git show gerrit/main:tests/unit/test_ci_provider_matrix.py | grep -c 30836378745` returns **0**.
All three rot-prone references are gone and main is green on the gate again.

I had a parallel fix up as Gerrit **1314**; it is now **ABANDONED** as superseded. It conflicted with
`36e986c188` on both files, and resolving the conflict to land a duplicate of work already on main
would have been pointless churn. The abandon message records the reason.

**Concrete cost this incident had, worth recording since it is the argument for the gate mattering:**
change 1311 took a `Verified -1` it did not cause, and I spent a cycle splitting my change in two to
work around a red main before discovering the fix was already in flight. A `main` that is red on a
gating job silently taxes every change in review.

Checking this ticket's own criteria against the landed fix:
 - [x] `check_comment_hygiene.py` exits 0 on main — verified above
 - [x] the three docstrings KEEP their explanation of why each test exists — `36e986c188` is a
       citation change, not a deletion
 - [x] the run id is replaced by a reference a reader can resolve (story f124)
 - [x] no test behaviour changed

Closing as **duplicate** — the defect was real and is fixed; this ticket simply is not the change
that fixed it.
